humanities_role_explanation: Distinct metric groups: standard CER/WER treat the 18th-century texts as content for a generic OCR task, while the novel HCPR and AIR metrics test period-specific disciplinary competence (diplomatic transcription, orthographic periodisation, detection of anachronistic 'over-historicization').
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Page/line images of 18th-century Russian Civil font books are input; models output text transcriptions compared to ground-truth text. Post-OCR correction experiments also use image plus OCR text or text only.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Diplomatic transcription (OCR) of historical Russian print in three modes (single line, full page, sliding window), plus post-OCR correction experiments. Historical Character Preservation Rate and Archaic Insertion Rate profile period-specific orthography and anachronisms; the paper also analyses error patterns and prompt-engineering effects.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task (OCR) on one corpus (18th-century Russian Civil font); a methodological framework with case study.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 12 multimodal LLMs: Claude 3.5/3.7, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o4-mini, Gemini 2.0/2.0-Flash-Lite/2.5 Flash/2.5 Pro, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Llama-4 Maverick/Scout.

quantitative_metrics.note: CER, WER, case-insensitive CER/WER, HCPR, AIR, CaseER, coefficient of variation.

summary: The paper proposes an evaluation methodology for LLM-based OCR of historical documents, with contamination-controlled data, new metrics (HCPR, AIR) and stability testing. It evaluates 12 multimodal LLMs on 1,029 pages of 18th-century Russian Civil font books, finding Gemini and Qwen best, a systematic 'over-historicization' error, and that post-OCR correction does not help.
key_findings: Gemini-2.5-Pro best in full-page mode (CER 3.36%, WER 4.69%) vs traditional OCR (Tesseract 21.55% CER, Transkribus PyLaia 26.93%, Surya 45.96% on a 100-page sample). Full-page mode is generally the best. Models over-historicize, inserting archaic characters (GPT-4o in 59% of files). Russian context-enhanced prompts reduce CER by up to 0.02. Text-only post-correction degrades performance.
facets_explanation: Ground truth was built via YOLOv8 layout analysis and fine-tuned TrOCR initial transcription, followed by 100% manual correction in eScriptorium under diplomatic principles by a single expert annotator in a two-pass protocol. A 500-line sample was audited by a second verifier (98.6% line exact match), treating residual disagreement as annotation error. The transcription is determined by the page image, scored against one reference text.
results_explanation: Table 3: Gemini-2.5-Pro 3.36 CER and 4.69 WER in full page mode. Largest mode gap is Gemini-2.5-Flash CER 4.94 (full page) vs 25.63 (sliding window), about 21 points; GPT-4o 9.23 vs 23.75 single line is about 15; the largest is Gemini-2.5-Flash 18.79 vs 4.94 single line (14). Reported gap in points was taken from Llama-4-Scout/other rows approximately and is the input-representation (processing mode) comparison. No human baseline is given; the 98.6% line-level agreement is annotator verification only.
